clue.text: Strategy in Ring opera, promoting right to take drugs?

indicators.note: promoting the R moves that letter from the back of the word up to the front

parts.note: to dope is to take drugs

explanation.surface: Someone sums up the plot of Wagner's Ring cycle as a scheme about pushing a drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like Wagner's operatic cycle, but it is the boxing ring and belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali's tactic of leaning on the ropes to let an opponent tire himself out is a famous boxing ploy.

clue.text: Severely criticise ruler getting upset about nothing

indicators.note: something upset is turned over, so the ruler's word is read from the bottom up in this down entry
about means going around, so the ruler's letters surround the nothing

parts.note: a tsar was the Russian emperor

explanation.surface: A monarch is attacked harshly by critics after getting upset over nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is informal for attacking or mocking them with harsh criticism.

clue.text: US criminal and others embracing universal proposal is an impossibility?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the others' word wraps around the universal letter

parts.note: et al is Latin for 'and others'
U is the film-classification letter for universal
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: An American crook's gang put forward a scheme that cannot possibly work.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine running forever without any energy input breaks the laws of thermodynamics, so it is the classic example of something unachievable; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Show Conservative military group beginning of Times Jumbo, say

parts.note: to air something is to show it in public

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

explanation.surface: A Tory military outfit promotes the start of the Times Jumbo crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times Jumbo is the newspaper's big crossword, but here Jumbo is the jumbo jet.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumbo jet, the nickname of the Boeing 747, is one example of a plane, hence 'say'.

clue.text: No longer interested in explorer's burn, perhaps

parts.note: to be over someone is to have lost interest in them
Captain James Cook, the navigator who charted the Pacific

explanation.surface: Someone has lost interest in the stream an explorer discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' reads as a noun, a Scottish stream belonging to the explorer, but it is the verb in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning food is one extreme way of cooking it for too long, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: In French, German artist's not finished last

indicators.note: something not finished lacks its end, so the final letter of the artist's name is lost

parts.note: Albrecht Dürer, the German Renaissance painter and engraver

explanation.surface: A German painter in France has not finished his work, coming in last.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or survive over time, a plain verb synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Comes to the trails of ships

definitions.meaning: first meaning: regains consciousness, stops sleeping
second meaning: the tracks of disturbed water left behind vessels

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests arriving at the trails left by boats; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper rouses on coming round, and boats leave turbulent tracks behind them in the water; both are the same word.

clue.text: Fancy reason to save instant messages

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it held inside, so the reason word holds the messages

parts.note: the why of something is its reason
IMs is the abbreviation for instant messages

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether there's a good reason to keep their chat history.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as a noun is a playful, capricious notion, which is what a whimsical idea is.

clue.text: Stay out of sight of ale, if people work drunk

indicators.note: drunk words stagger about out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Keep hidden from the beer if workers turn up drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying out of public notice and avoiding attention is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Machine packing seed for bird

indicators.note: packing means stuffing something inside, so the machine word holds the seed

parts.note: a power tool for smoothing wood
a pip is a fruit seed

explanation.surface: A machine stuffed with seed to feed the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a small long-billed wader that runs along shorelines, a specific species of bird.

clue.text: Exposed to elements endlessly in Scottish town?

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the phrase's final letter is lost

parts.note: something left out to dry in the open air

explanation.surface: Someone is constantly exposed to wind and rain in a damp Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Airdrie is a town in North Lanarkshire, east of Glasgow; the question mark nods at Scotland's wet weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a real place in central Scotland, an example of a town there.

clue.text: Doctor beginning to isolate blood vessel outside theatre

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: a vein carries blood back to the heart

explanation.surface: A doctor starts isolating a vein outside an operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' and 'theatre' seem to place the medical scene; together they define an open-air cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-in is an open-air cinema watched from parked cars, a theatre out of doors.

clue.text: Third person's at that location reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, pointing to how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: the adverb for that place, said out loud

explanation.surface: Someone describes where a third party is, as reported.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun for 'they' belongs to the third person plural, so it is the third person's word for belonging.

clue.text: Eccentric and intelligent cheat

parts.note: a card is an amusingly odd person

explanation.surface: A description of a quirky, clever swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a swindler who wins at poker and similar games by trickery.

clue.text: Tobacco container put out next to TV

parts.note: to snuff a candle is to extinguish it
the box is slang for the television

explanation.surface: A tin of tobacco has been set down beside the television.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lidded case holds powdered tobacco that is sniffed rather than smoked.

clue.text: Sub confused with advice to submerge with tank?

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled up, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A submarine crew, muddled by instructions, is told to go under with a tank.
explanation.walkthrough: The tank sounds military, beside a submarine, but it is the air cylinder on a diver's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers carry a cylinder of compressed air as they swim underwater, so going under with one is this sport.

clue.text: Attempt to seize power company at an end

explanation.surface: A takeover bid for a business that is finished anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'état is a sudden, often violent overthrow of a government by a small group.

clue.text: Brief time running banks

indicators.note: banks are the edges either side of a river, so this word wraps around the time

explanation.surface: A short spell of time spent jogging along riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brief passes quickly and soon vanishes, which is what a transient moment does.

clue.text: Programme is on a lease — that's clear

parts.note: an app is a computer program

explanation.surface: A broadcast show has been rented out, and that is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Programme' suggests television, but it is a piece of software.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious or plainly visible is evident to all, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Unpleasant in a self-satisfied way, ignoring two leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters, and ignoring two of them drops the opening pair

explanation.surface: Someone behaves smugly and disagreeably while snubbing a pair of bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly scene or mood is nasty and threatening, so the word extends to anything disagreeable.

clue.text: Shrewd publication is a buzzkill?

parts.note: fly is British slang for knowing and sharp

explanation.surface: A clever magazine turns out to be a party pooper.
explanation.walkthrough: A buzzkill is slang for a spoilsport; here it is read literally as something that kills buzzing insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky strips hung up to trap insects literally kill the things that buzz.

clue.text: One regulation I'd set up for religious festival

indicators.note: set up in a down entry means raised, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone plans to establish a rule for a holy day.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights celebrated each autumn, a religious holiday.

clue.text: Passed down directly from new alien vessel's base

indicators.note: new means freshly made, so these letters take a fresh order
in a down entry the base is the bottom, so the final letter is kept

explanation.surface: Something inherited directly from the bottom of a new alien spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineal describes descent in an unbroken line from parent to child, as with inheritance.

clue.text: Go out with Iberian native

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone starts dating a Spanish or Portuguese local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out with' reads as one phrase for dating; it splits into fodder, signal and link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is an original inhabitant of a land, someone indigenous to the place.

clue.text: Steer clear of area with invalid

explanation.surface: Keep away from a place where a sick person lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' suggests a sick person; it is the adjective meaning null.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep away from something or shun it is a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: City Democrat also called Republican

parts.note: aka is short for 'also known as'

explanation.surface: A politician from one American party is also known as a member of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Dakar is the capital of Senegal in West Africa, an example of a city.

clue.text: Caught in net, a timid, recoiling ape

indicators.note: recoiling means springing backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
caught in means held inside, so the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A shy monkey flinches after being trapped in a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like the animal in the net, but it is the verb meaning copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy their behaviour, a verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Pleasant heading off to choose climbing tool

indicators.note: the heading is the first letter, and taking it off drops it

explanation.surface: A pleasant person sets off to select gear for a climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountaineer uses a small spiked axe to cut footholds in frozen slopes.

clue.text: Lean on pupil occasionally showing boredom

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A teacher who now and then puts pressure on a student reveals how bored they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loan for listless weariness and dissatisfaction, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Lethargy when running around India for a great distance

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the India letter
running suggests letters moving about loosely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Sluggishness sets in when jogging around India over a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit measures how far light travels in twelve months, about six trillion miles, an enormous stretch.
